title.ru: План грамматики B2 с ChatGPT — неделя 1

sessions.mainFocus: Choose -ing or to + verb after common verbs and expressions.

blocks.instruction: Complete five sentences without checking the rule.
Study the patterns and compare the examples.
Complete Exercises 1 and 2.
Answer the prompts aloud using the target patterns.
Correct mistakes and save three personal examples.

rules.rule: Use verb + -ing after enjoy, avoid, mention, suggest, finish and keep.
Use verb + to-infinitive after decide, hope, plan, want, need and promise.
examples: I plan to apply for jobs.
We decided to stay in New Zealand.

rules.rule: Use -ing after prepositions and expressions such as How about... ?
examples: I'm interested in improving my pronunciation.

exercises.instruction: Use the correct form of the verb in brackets.

items.prompt: I avoid ___ English only in class. (speak)
We decided ___ a different course. (try)
How about ___ the answer again? (explain)
He mentioned ___ late. (arrive)
I hope ___ more confidently soon. (speak)

exercises.instruction: Answer aloud in two or three sentences.

items.prompt: What do you enjoy doing in Auckland?
What do you plan to do when your English reaches B2?
Suggest an English activity for tonight.

vocabulary.example: I’m trying to figure out which form sounds right.
It is easier to keep up when I study regularly.
I’m not completely sure, but I’ll give it a go.

sessions.topic: Present Perfect vs Present Perfect Continuous
sessions.mainFocus: Contrast completed results with duration or ongoing activity.

blocks.instruction: Recall Session 1 patterns and say three examples.
Compare result, duration and repeated activity.
Complete Exercise 2a.
Describe your life and English study using both tenses.
Ask ChatGPT for direct corrections and repeat each corrected sentence.

rules.rule: Use Present Perfect for a result, completed amount or life experience.
examples: I've completed four lessons this week.

rules.rule: Use Present Perfect Continuous for duration, an unfinished activity or visible recent activity.
examples: I've been studying for two hours.
It's wet because it has been raining.

rules.rule: Some state verbs normally use the simple form, not the continuous form.
examples: I've known her for ten years.
I've wanted to improve my English for a long time.

exercises.instruction: Complete each sentence with the best tense.

items.prompt: I ___ three grammar exercises today. (finish)
I ___ English since breakfast. (study)
How long ___ you ___ in Auckland? (live)
I ___ that word several times this week. (use)
She ___ him since university. (know)

exercises.instruction: Speak for two minutes. Include at least two examples of each tense.
exercises.prompt: What have you achieved since moving to New Zealand, and what have you been working on recently?

vocabulary.example: I've studied for four hours so far this week.
I've been making progress with spontaneous speaking.
We've been settling into life in Auckland.

sessions.mainFocus: Express real and hypothetical consequences accurately.

blocks.instruction: Review two errors from Sessions 1 and 2.
Compare first, second and third conditionals.
Complete Exercises 3a and 3b.
Answer hypothetical questions without writing first.
Build a three-card error review set.

rules.rule: First conditional: if/unless + present, will + base verb for a realistic future result.
examples: If I practise daily, I'll improve.
I won't improve unless I speak regularly.

rules.rule: Second conditional: if + past, would + base verb for a hypothetical present or future.
examples: If I had more confidence, I would speak more.

rules.rule: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle for an unreal past.
examples: If I had practised earlier, I would have felt calmer.

rules.rule: Otherwise introduces the consequence if the previous action does not happen.
examples: Write the phrase down; otherwise, you may forget it.

items.prompt: If I don't practise speaking, I won't become confident. Use unless.
items.answer: I won't become confident unless I practise speaking.

items.prompt: Leave now, or you will miss the bus. Use otherwise.
items.answer: Leave now; otherwise, you will miss the bus.

items.prompt: I didn't prepare, so I felt nervous. Use the third conditional.
items.answer: If I had prepared, I wouldn't have felt nervous.

items.prompt: What will happen if you practise speaking every day?
What would you do if you got a job interview tomorrow?
What would have been different if you had started speaking practice earlier?

vocabulary.example: You won't remember it unless you use it.
Practise aloud; otherwise, recognition will not become active speech.
I'll sort out the appointment tomorrow.

sessions.mainFocus: Retrieve this week's grammar quickly in realistic New Zealand situations.

blocks.instruction: Explain the three grammar topics without looking at notes.
Complete Exercise 4a.
Role-play a job interview, café conversation and phone call with ChatGPT.
Repeat corrected sentences, then change one detail in each.
Mark each topic: Know, Hard or Again.

items.prompt: I enjoy to speak with native speakers.
items.answer: I enjoy speaking with native speakers.

items.prompt: I've studied for two hours and I'm not finished yet.
items.answer: I've been studying for two hours and I'm not finished yet.

items.prompt: Unless I will practise, I won't improve.
items.answer: Unless I practise, I won't improve.

items.prompt: If I would have more confidence, I would apply now.
items.answer: If I had more confidence, I would apply now.

items.prompt: She mentioned to move to Wellington.

exercises.instruction: Speak immediately. Do not write a script.

items.prompt: A recruiter asks what you have been doing since moving to New Zealand.

weeklySuccessCriteria: Score at least 80 percent on the mixed review after corrections.
Use six target structures during unscripted speaking.
Recall at least eight new expressions without revealing the translation.
Save no more than five recurring errors for next week's spaced review.
